newsitem.title: USA: Credit union ruling to be appealed to Supreme Court.
newsitem.headline: Credit union ruling to be appealed to Supreme Court.

text.p: The Department of Justice will ask the Supreme Court to review whether credit unions can add members from unrelated industry groups, the regulator of credit unions said Friday.

U.S. Solicitor General Walter Dillinger said he will soon ask the Supreme Court to review a July appeals court ruling that the National Credit Union Administration's membership and expansion policy is illegal, the group said.
The NCUA, the federal regulator of credit unions, in the early 1980s began allowing credit unions to take in members from various industries.
Bankers sued the NCUA for allowing credit unions to add members from unrelated fields, saying the practice violated the 1934 Federal Credit Union Act.

Credit unions are non-profit organisations that generally offer lower rates on loans and higher savings rates than banks. They enjoy tax advantages that banks contend have given them unfair advantages, allowing the favourable terms.

In another court ruling, the U.S. District Court last month said credit unions could not add any more groups that were unrelated to the original employee group nor new members from existing non-related groups.
The Department of Justice, acting on behalf of the NCUA, Friday asked the U.S. District Court to lift the nationwide injuction it issued Oct. 25, NCUA said.
"Should the stay be granted, federal credit unions would be allowed to continue operating as they had been, pending possible review of the case by the high court," NCUA said.
